description: Seven cannabis branding agencies, each re-checked in October 2026, plus an honest guide to when an agency is right and when a senior freelancer is the better hire.
body:
A cannabis branding agency is a firm that builds the logo, packaging, signage and website for a dispensary or cannabis product brand, inside an industry where almost all paid advertising is banned.

That ban is why the brief is different here: the pack and the store have to do the work a campaign would do in any other category.

I’m Arek Dvornechuck, a senior freelance brand designer in New York, and I designed the identity and packaging for SweetGrass, a premium dispensary in Mississippi, and the rebrand for Medihuanna, an accredited medicinal cannabis education provider in Sydney.

So I have an obvious interest here, and I’d rather be upfront about it than pretend otherwise.

This page does two things: it lists seven cannabis branding agencies I checked by hand in October 2026, and it says plainly when hiring an agency is the right call and when a senior freelancer is the better one.

The previous version of this list had nine firms on it, and four of them no longer stand up, so I removed them and said why.

Key takeaways

  • Pick on scope, not on agency size: a dispensary launch and a single product line are different jobs with different right answers.
  • An agency earns its fee when you need many things at once — packaging plus paid media plus a dispensary menu plus photography.
  • A senior freelancer wins when you mainly need the brand itself done well, quickly, by the person who actually designs it.
  • None of these firms publish their rates, so pin down scope and deliverables in writing before you talk about money.
  • Ask every candidate the same compliance question, because the ones who have shipped in your state answer it in specifics.

Jump to the part you need.

  • Deciding who to hire: agency, studio or freelancer, then what it costs.
  • Shopping the market: the seven agencies, then how to vet them.
  • Working with one designer: the freelance alternative.
  • Checking an old bookmark: the four I removed, then the FAQ.

Agency, studio or senior freelancer?

Most people searching for a cannabis branding agency have not actually decided they need an agency — they have decided they need help.

Those are different conclusions, and the cost gap between them is large.

Hire a full-service cannabis agency when:

  • You are opening a dispensary and need the brand, the build-out signage, the menu integration, photography and paid media moving in parallel.
  • You need ongoing marketing after launch, not a one-time identity.
  • You are a multi-state operator and need someone tracking different rules in each market.
  • You have the budget to carry a team and the time to run an engagement measured in months.

Hire a senior freelancer when:

  • The thing you actually need is the brand itself — logo, palette, typography, packaging, guidelines — done once and done properly.
  • You want the person who designs it to be the person you talk to.
  • You need it in weeks rather than quarters, because a licence window or a harvest is already moving.
  • You would rather spend the rest of the budget on product and build-out than on account management.

The honest version of the trade-off: an agency buys you breadth, a freelancer buys you the senior hand.

At an agency, the person who pitched you is rarely the person who draws your wordmark, and that is not a scandal — it is simply how the model works.

If breadth is what you need, that model is worth paying for.

What cannabis branding costs in 2026

None of the seven agencies below publish their pricing, so treat any figure you read on a listicle — including the one this page used to carry — as a guess.

What you can do is control the shape of the quote.

  • Ask for a fixed scope, not an hourly rate, so a slow month is their problem and not your invoice.
  • Ask what is excluded, because packaging dielines, print-ready files and photography are the usual surprises.
  • Ask who owns the files at the end, in writing.
  • Ask how many products the packaging price covers, since cannabis SKUs multiply fast.

For reference, my own rate is published and flat: $3,000 per week, with a cannabis brand identity delivered in one week, guaranteed.

I mention it only so you have one real number to measure quotes against.

7 cannabis branding agencies, checked in October 2026

I opened every one of these sites in October 2026 and took the details below from the firms’ own pages, so where a claim is theirs I have said so.

They are ordered by how much of their work is brand and packaging design rather than media buying, because that is what this page is about.

1. Wick & Mortar

The most design-led firm on this list, and the one that has been doing it longest.

Wick & Mortar describes itself as “A Full-Service Creative Branding & Marketing Agency, Highly-Focused on Plant Medicine,” and says it has been “crafting, creating and cultivating cannabis brands” since 2009.

It works out of Los Angeles and covers branding, packaging, web design, photography, copywriting and strategy.

Its published work includes Goldkine, Hitoki, Olswell, Cultivera, Narvona, Harmony Farms, Spoil’d, ZoZ and Dose.

It also runs courses and a podcast, which is a reasonable way to judge whether you like how they think before you pay them anything.

Good fit if you want packaging and identity treated as the main event rather than as assets for a media plan.

2. PufCreativ

The broadest client roster of any firm here, and one of the few that lists packaging as a standing service.

PufCreativ calls itself “An Award-Winning, Community-Focused Cannabis Marketing Agency.”

Its services run across web design, branding, packaging, photography, loyalty, social media, advertising, and SEO and AI visibility.

The client logos on its site include Rebel Spirit Cannabis, Pure Options, Story Cannabis, Jardin Las Vegas, The Travel Agency, Shore House Canna, Newport Cannabis, Sol Flower, Buddies and 40 Tons.

The site does not name a headquarters, so ask where the team actually sits if that matters to you.

Good fit if you are a multi-location operator who wants one firm across brand, packaging and retention.

3. Cannabis Creative Group

A full-stack firm whose brand work sits beside some genuinely cannabis-specific plumbing.

Note the name: older listicles file this firm under “Cannabis Marketing Agency,” but it trades as Cannabis Creative Group, out of Newton, Massachusetts.

Its services cover brand identity, print and packaging design, web design and development, digital advertising, SEO, social media, email, SMS, public relations, photography and video, and a dispensary launch package.

The native dispensary menu SEO is the unusual one, because menu pages are where a lot of dispensary traffic actually lands.

Named clients and testimonials on the site include Full Harvest Moonz, Canna Companion, KELIA, Clebby’s, Emerald Grove, Drops of Life, Upstate Elevator Supply and ACT Lab.

Good fit if you are opening a dispensary and want the menu and the brand handled by the same team.

4. CannaPlanners

The strongest website-first option, with branding and packaging attached.

CannaPlanners describes itself as “a cannabis marketing agency specializing in web design, SEO & retention marketing,” and works out of Burlington, Vermont.

Alongside the web work it offers branding, logo design and packaging design.

Its published case studies and testimonials name Silver Therapeutics, Klutch Cannabis, Nostalgia, Sunday Goods and Yellowbird, and the site says it is “trusted by hundreds of cannabis companies.”

Its homepage press strip shows Rolling Stone, Forbes, mg Magazine, Marijuana Venture, GreenState and Seven Days.

Good fit if your immediate bottleneck is the website and the online menu rather than the logo.

5. Hybrid Marketing Co

A dispensary-heavy agency where branding sits inside a performance marketing practice.

Hybrid Marketing Co works out of Denver and says that “since 2015, we have worked with dispensaries, cannabis brands, hemp companies, and B2B operators across the United States.”

Branding and design is one of eight services, beside SEO and SEM, paid media, social, email and SMS, web development, content and strategy.

Its testimonials come from CUE Cannabis, Rooted Ridge Nursery, Vanguard Cannabis and Lightshade, and its client logos include Cheech & Chong, Azuca, Wana Wellness, Sol Flower, Timber Cannabis Co and MJ Unpacked.

If you want a brand built in isolation, this is probably not the shape you need.

Good fit if you already have traffic and want brand work in service of measurable growth.

6. Herban Creative

The East Coast option, with offices in three states.

Herban Creative trades as a cannabis marketing agency across New Jersey, New York and Florida, with its headquarters in Morristown, New Jersey.

Its services are web design, branding, digital marketing, SEO, social media, email marketing, CTV advertising, photography and videography, and a dedicated dispensary marketing practice.

Projects listed on its site include Curaleaf, Goliath Nutrition, June’s Moon, Dankorations, Aeterna and Uzuri Hand & Foot Spa.

The CTV advertising line is worth noting, because connected-TV is one of the few paid channels some operators can still reach.

Good fit if you are operating in the New Jersey, New York or Florida markets and want someone local to them.

7. High Rise

The largest by volume, and the most marketing-led of the seven.

High Rise calls itself “The World’s Leading Cannabis Marketing Agency” and says it has been “trusted by the biggest names in cannabis since 2012,” with 500+ clients.

Older listicles, this one included, used to date the firm to 2018; its own site says 2012.

Its services are content creation, digital interfaces, awareness, strategy and influencer marketing.

It names no clients on its homepage, so ask for relevant work in your category and your state before signing anything.

Good fit if you need a high volume of content and campaign assets rather than a ground-up identity.

The freelance alternative

Every firm above is an agency, which means a team, an account layer and a timeline measured in months.

For a lot of cannabis founders that is more machine than the job requires.

I work the other way round: one senior designer, one flat weekly rate, and the brand identity finished in a week.

For SweetGrass, a premium dispensary in Mississippi, that meant an Art Deco-inspired wordmark, custom typography, seamless patterns, a packaging system across jars, droppers and retail bags, a brochure, billboards and the website.

For Medihuanna in Sydney it meant a full rebrand for an accredited medicinal cannabis education provider.

The part that matters most in this category is how the packaging gets drawn.

I block out the regulated panel at real size first — warnings, symbol, batch number, THC and CBD content, the QR code — and then design the brand into whatever surface is left.

Done the other way round, the brand looks beautiful in the deck and falls apart the moment the compliance text lands on it.

Where a freelancer is the wrong answer: if you need paid media, influencer campaigns, ongoing social and photography on retainer, hire one of the agencies above instead.

I design brands; I do not run campaigns.

If the brand itself is the job, see how cannabis branding works with me, or read the longer guide to cannabis branding and 12 examples.

How to vet a cannabis branding agency

Shortlist three firms, ask all three the same five things, and compare the answers rather than the portfolios.

  • Ask which states they have shipped packaging in. A firm that has done it in your state will name the rule, not the feeling.
  • Ask to see a label at real size. A pack that only exists as a hero render has never met a compliance panel.
  • Ask who does the drawing. Get the name of the designer, not the name of the account lead.
  • Ask what happens when the rules change. Labels get revised; find out whether that is covered or billed.
  • Ask for one reference you did not find on their site. The clients a firm volunteers are its best ones by definition.

One more, which sounds blunt but saves months: ask what they would refuse to design for you.

A firm that has shipped in this category will have an immediate answer, usually involving a green leaf.

Four agencies I removed from this list

This list ran for two years with nine firms on it, and in October 2026 I checked each one and found four that no longer belong.

If you arrived here from an older bookmark, this is where they went.

  • Highly Creative — the domain no longer resolves. It was also listed here as my own agency, which was never an accurate description of how I work: I am a senior freelance designer, not a firm with a team.
  • Highopes — highopes.co now returns a 404.
  • Brandjoint — merged into Peppermill Projects, which describes itself as brand strategy for founders, entrepreneurs and small businesses, with no stated cannabis focus.
  • Bluedream — not an agency at all. bluedream.com is an independent strain-guide site published by Official Cannabis in Valencia, Spain, and it states plainly that it does not sell cannabis or seeds.

I also corrected several client lists that earlier versions of this page carried but that the firms themselves do not publish.

Cannabis branding agencies: FAQ

How much does a cannabis branding agency cost?

None of the seven agencies on this list publish their rates, so the only honest answer is that you have to ask for a fixed scope in writing. My own published rate is $3,000 per week, flat, with a cannabis brand identity delivered in one week.

Do I need a cannabis-specific agency, or will any branding agency do?

You need someone who has shipped packaging under a state cannabis regime, because the regulated panel decides the layout before the brand does. That experience can come from an agency or from an individual designer, but it cannot come from a generalist who has never read your state’s rules.

What is the difference between a cannabis branding agency and a cannabis marketing agency?

A branding agency builds the identity, packaging and brand system; a marketing agency buys and runs media against it. Several firms on this list do both, which is useful if you need both and expensive if you only need the first.

How long does cannabis branding take?

At an agency, typically two to six months depending on scope and how many approval layers sit between you and the designer. Working with me it is one week for the brand identity, guaranteed, with packaging and the website scoped separately at the same weekly rate.

Can a branding agency guarantee my packaging is compliant?

No, and be careful with any that says it can, because the final legal responsibility for the label sits with the licence holder. What a good designer does is build the layout around your state’s required elements at real size so the artwork never fights the rules.

Is a freelancer riskier than an agency?

The real risk in either case is seniority, not headcount. At an agency you may get a junior designer you never met; with a freelancer you get exactly the person whose portfolio you reviewed, which is the whole point.

Choosing between them

If you need breadth — packaging and paid media and photography and a dispensary menu, all moving together — hire one of the seven agencies above, and use the five questions to pick.

If what you actually need is the brand done properly, once, by the designer you spoke to, that is the job I do.

One week, $3,000 flat, guaranteed — see cannabis branding and packaging design.
